outputs.exact_statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity $\nu$ on the unit flat torus $\mathbb T^3$. There is an algorithm taking a deterministic one-tape machine $M$ with head moves in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and a finite input word $w$ to an effective smooth force $f_{M,w}$ with these properties.* 1. *The force is divergence free and has zero spatial mean. Equation [eq:NS] has a global smooth solution $(u,p)=(U,0)$, unique in the classical class just specified on every finite time interval.* 2. *All mixed derivatives of $U$ and $f_{M,w}$ are globally bounded, and the kinetic energy is uniformly bounded. Both fields have period one for $t\ge1$ and vanish on a neighborhood of every integer time. The period-one mechanism after initialization depends on $M$ alone.* 3. *With fixed label $a_*=(1/8,3/8,1/2)$ and fixed open strip $O=\{(x,y,z):1/20$, the same formulas and conclusions hold; the evaluation algorithm is then relative to that parameter.

For the machine just specified there is a finite partial one-head transition table satisfying these properties on its entire allowed domain:*

1.  *Each destination control has a fixed incoming displacement.*

2.  *The destination control and the written complete symbol determine the preceding control and the read complete symbol.*


*Initialize its work track with a prescribed finite input, its head at zero, and its control at $S_q$, where $q$ is the original initial state. For any integer $r_0\ge2$, put the history frontier at $r_0$, empty history elsewhere, and mark zero at every cell. At the $n$th checkpoint it represents exactly the original configuration after $n$ instructions, and its frontier is at $r_0+n$. If that original instruction has next head position $h'$, the next checkpoint is reached after exactly $$\label{eq:count}
 2(r_0+n-h')+4$$ local transitions. A nonhalting original run gives an indefinitely defined recorder run, and a halting checkpoint is reached exactly when the original machine halts.

For $1\le i\le N$, let $P_i,Q_i$ be closed axis-parallel rectangles with rational endpoints and positive side lengths in the planar chart of $\mathbb T_L^3$. Let their centers be $p_i,q_i$, and suppose $$F_i(X)=q_i+\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i,\lambda_i^{-1})(X-p_i), \quad F_i(P_i)=Q_i, \quad\lambda_i\in\mathbb Q_{>0}.$$ Assume the following:* 1. *The $P_i$ are pairwise positively separated, and the $Q_i$ are pairwise positively separated.* 2. *Every coordinate half-width of every $P_i$ and $Q_i$ is at most a given rational $h>0$.* 3. *All $p_i,q_i$ belong to a closed rectangle $K$ with rational endpoints, and $K+[-2h,2h]^2$ is compactly contained in the planar chart.* 4. *The coding height $z_0$ is rational and lies inside the vertical chart.* *There is an effectively constructed smooth velocity $V$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T_L^3$ with the following properties.* 1. *It is one-periodic in time and vanishes near every integer time. Every mixed space and time derivative has an effective uniform bound.* 2. *$\operatorname{div}V=0$, $\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}V=0$, and $(V\cdot\nabla)V=0$.* 3. *Its period map is $(X,z)\mapsto(F_i(X),z)$ on an effectively specified positive neighborhood of each $P_i\times\{z_0\}$.* 4. *Starting from $(X,z_0)$ with $X\in P_i$, the four scaling stages stay within horizontal sup distance $2h$ of $p_i$. The next stage follows $((1-\theta)p_i+\theta q_i)+d$, where $0\le\theta\le1$ and $|d|_\infty\le h$. The lifting and lowering stages leave $X$ unchanged.* 5. *For each fixed positive computable $\nu$, the force $f=\partial_tV-\nu\Delta V$ is smooth, mean zero, and solenoidal, with period one and bounded mixed derivatives. Equation [eq:NS] from zero initial velocity has the solution $(u,p)=(V,0)$, with uniformly bounded kinetic energy. This solution is unique among spatially periodic classical solutions for which $u$, its spatial derivatives through order two, $u_t$, $p$, and $\nabla p$ are continuous on each finite closed time cylinder, and $p$ has zero spatial mean at each time.* *No separation between a source and a target is required. For $N=0$ the zero velocity has all the asserted properties, with no branch conditions.

Under Theorem 4, suppose a branch satisfies $p_{i,1},q_{i,1}\le a$. Every point starting in $P_i\times\{z_0\}$ has first coordinate at most $a+2h$ throughout the period. If instead both centers are at least $a$, its first coordinate is at least $a-2h$. If $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb T_L^3$ is open and $Q_i\times\{z_0\}\subseteq\mathcal O$, every point starting in $P_i\times\{z_0\}$ reaches $\mathcal O$ at the integer sample and remains there for a time interval.

The finite families $(P_i)$ and $(Q_i)$ are separately pairwise positively separated, with gap at least $\kappa/B^2$ in some coordinate for every pair. Their side lengths are positive, rational, and at most $\kappa$. No source–target separation is asserted or needed.
No algorithm decides the event of Theorem 1 for every finite force prescription produced by its compiler.

The chronological list $$\mathsf X(\lambda^{-1}-1),\quad \mathsf Y(1),\quad \mathsf X(\lambda-1),\quad \mathsf Y(-\lambda^{-1})$$ has the successive endpoints $$\begin{aligned} &(r+(\lambda^{-1}-1)s,s),\\ &(r+(\lambda^{-1}-1)s,r+s/\lambda),\\ &(\lambda r,r+s/\lambda),\\ &(\lambda r,s/\lambda). \end{aligned}$$ The proof of Lemma 3 bounds each coordinate by $2h$; convexity handles partial shears. Replacing the four middle scaling fields accordingly preserves the rest of Theorem 4. Alternatively, split $W_6$ into its two horizontal components and give them successive unit-integral pulses. This gives eight stages with one Cartesian component active at a time. The horizontal center now moves first in one coordinate and then in the other. Both segments stay in the rectangle $K$, so the coordinate bounds and the proof of Corollary 5 persist. Every field is still transverse, mean zero, and free of self-advection. This variant has the same endpoint map, although its translation path differs.

Fix $ u>0$ and $\Omega\in\{\mathbb T^3,\mathbb R^3,\mathbb R^2 imes\mathbb T\}$. Let $U$ be smooth and divergence free on $[0,\infty) imes\Omega$, with $U(0)=0$, and suppose $U$ and $ abla U$ are bounded on every finite closed time cylinder. In the noncompact cases assume the velocity conditions in [eq:energy-class]. Then the force $$\mathcal F_ u[U]=U_t+(U\cdot abla)U- u\Delta U$$ has the solution $(u,p)=(U,0)$, unique in the classical class just defined on each finite time interval. Its material trajectories exist uniquely for every finite time. On $\mathbb T^3$, mean-zero $U$ gives mean-zero $\mathcal F_ u[U]$.* *More generally, if an independently constructed pair $(U,P)$ is a classical solution in the same class for a given force and initial velocity, it is the unique solution for those data in that class. In either noncompact uniqueness statement, the competitor’s gradient bound can be omitted while keeping its bounded velocity and all other conditions. The reference velocity $U$ still has bounded gradient. For smooth $U$, each finite-time material map $\Phi_t$ is a smooth diffeomorphism and satisfies $$U(t,\cdot)=(\partial_t\Phi_t)\circ\Phi_t^{-1},\qquad \partial_{tt}\Phi_t(a) =(f- abla P+ u\Delta U)(t,\Phi_t(a)).$$
